2610.06804.title: Sharpen Without Search: On-Policy Distillation of Sequence-Level Power Distribution
2610.06804.paper_summary: A language model can give a correct answer more probability than any single incorrect answer and still usually sample an incorrect one, because the incorrect answers together hold more probability. The power distribution raises each complete answer's probability to a power above one and renormalizes, shifting probability toward answers the model finds most likely (sharpening). Sampling from it improves reasoning without changing parameters, but needs many scored candidates per query. We show that a model can instead be trained to produce such answers in one generation. On-policy power distillation (OPPD) runs a sequential Monte Carlo sampler in which the model being trained generates candidates and a frozen teacher's power distribution weights them; the same probabilities weight each answer in a maximum-likelihood update. Training raises single-generation accuracy by up to 23.0 points on MATH500 and 27.3 on GSM8K over the untrained model at the same temperature, and one generation scores 2.4 and 3.5 points above published power sampling with 64 candidates, recovering 94 percent of the gain that 16 candidates give the untrained model. For context, against GRPO trained with verified rewards from the same checkpoint and budget, OPPD scores 3.8, 4.0 and 5.4 points higher on MATH500, GSM8K and AIME using no reference answers; the two are complementary, and OPPD applied after GRPO adds up to 9.3 points. Trained only on mathematics, OPPD raises HumanEval accuracy by up to 5.3 points. One loss coefficient moves the sharpening exponent the model absorbs between 1.19 and 2.02, against 1.14 for ordinary on-policy distillation, and it rises mostly on the model's own answers. Gains hold across model families and sizes, including a model already trained with verified rewards, where lowering the temperature gives nothing and OPPD adds 4.4 points on MATH500. Code: https://github.com/ArminAzizi98/OPPD.
2610.06804.paper_summary_zh: 語言模型可以給出正確答案的概率高於任何單一的錯誤答案，並且通常仍然會抽樣到錯誤的答案，因為錯誤答案的總體概率更高。權力分佈將每個完整答案的概率提升到一個高於一的指數並重新正規化，將概率轉移到模型認為最可能的答案上（鋒利化）。從中抽樣可以改善推理而不改變參數，但每個查詢需要許多有分數的候選者。我們展示了一種模型可以被訓練以在一次生成中產生這樣的答案。政策內部的權力蒸餾（OPPD）運行一個序列蒙特卡羅抽樣器，其中正在訓練的模型生成候選者，並且一個固定教師的權力分佈對它們進行加權；在最大似然更新中，每個答案的概率相同。訓練使單代準確度在 MATH500 上提高了最多 23.0 分，在 GSM8K 上提高了 27.3 分，相比於在相同溫度下的未訓練模型，而一次生成的得分比使用 64 個候選者的已發表權力抽樣高出 2.4 和 3.5 分，恢復了未訓練模型使用 16 個候選者所帶來的 94% 的增益。為了提供背景，與從相同檢查點和預算中獲得驗證獎勵的 GRPO 相比，OPPD 在 MATH500、GSM8K 和 AIME 上的得分分別高出 3.8、4.0 和 5.4 分，未使用任何參考答案；這兩者是互補的，OPPD 在 GRPO 之後應用總共增加了 9.3 分。僅在數學上進行訓練的 OPPD 將 HumanEval 的準確率提高了最多 5.3 分。一個損失係數使模型吸收的鋒利化指數在 1.19 和 2.02 之間變化，而普通的政策蒸餾則為 1.14，並且主要在模型自己的答案上上升。增益在模型系列和大小之間保持一致，包括已經用驗證獎勵訓練的模型，降低溫度則沒有任何效果，而 OPPD 在 MATH500 上增加了 4.4 分。代碼：https://github.com/ArminAzizi98/OPPD。
